questions.text: Based on the table below showing major soil types in India and their characteristics, which soil type is correctly matched with its characteristic feature and dominant crop? Soil Type | Characteristic Feature | Dominant Crop | Major States Alluvial | Light grey, fertile | Rice, Wheat | UP, Bihar, Punjab Black (Regur) | Clayey, cracks in summer | Cotton | Maharashtra, MP Red | Porous, friable, iron oxide | Millets, Groundnut | TN, Karnataka Laterite | Leached, acidic, Fe/Al oxides | Tea, Cashew | Kerala, Karnataka, Odisha

options.label: A
options.text: Alluvial - Clayey, cracks in summer - Cotton

options.label: C
options.text: Red - Porous, friable, iron oxide - Millets

questions.solution: Shortcut: Locate the row for 'Red' soil in the table. Verify that the 'Characteristic Feature' (Porous, friable, iron oxide) and 'Dominant Crop' (Millets, Groundnut) match Option C exactly. Step-by-step: Option A describes Black soil features for Alluvial. Option B describes Alluvial features for Black soil. Option D lists Wheat for Laterite (Tea/Cashew are correct). Only Option C matches the table data for Red soil perfectly.

questions.text: With reference to the Fundamental Duties enshrined in Article 51A of the Constitution of India, consider the following statements: 1. They were incorporated by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. 2. The duty to provide opportunities for education to children between the age of six and fourteen years was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002. 3. Unlike Directive Principles, Fundamental Duties are legally enforceable by courts through writ jurisdiction. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the 'Enforceability' elimination trick. Statement 3 claims Fundamental Duties are legally enforceable by courts. This is factually incorrect; they are non-justiciable (non-enforceable by courts), unlike Fundamental Rights. Eliminate options containing Statement 3 (B, C, D). Only Option A remains. Full Solution: Statement 1 is correct: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added Part IVA (Article 51A) based on the Swaran Singh Committee report. Statement 2 is correct: The 86th Amendment (2002) added clause (k) regarding education for children aged 6-14. Statement 3 is incorrect: Fundamental Duties are moral obligations, not legally enforceable by writs.

questions.text: As per the table below showing State-wise Installed Solar and Wind Power Capacity (in MW) as of March 2023, which state has the highest ratio of Solar Capacity to Wind Capacity?
questions.solution: Shortcut: A ratio > 1 requires Solar > Wind. Only Rajasthan (18,000 > 5,000) and Karnataka (8,000 > 6,000) qualify. Compare 18/5 (3.6) vs 8/6 (1.33); Rajasthan is higher. Worked: Gujarat=10,000/11,000≈0.91; Rajasthan=18,000/5,000=3.6; Tamil Nadu=7,000/10,000=0.7; Karnataka=8,000/6,000≈1.33. Highest is Rajasthan.

questions.text: Consider the following statements regarding the 'National Green Tribunal (NGT)': 1. It was established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 for effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to environmental protection. 2. The Tribunal is bound by the procedure laid down under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. 3. Appeals against orders of the NGT lie directly to the Supreme Court of India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use 'Natural Justice vs CPC' and 'Appellate Hierarchy' rules. Statement 1: Correct. NGT Act, 2010 established it for environmental justice. Statement 2: Incorrect. Section 19 of NGT Act explicitly states the Tribunal is *not* bound by CPC, 1908, but guided by principles of natural justice. Statement 3: Correct. Section 22 provides for appeal to Supreme Court within 90 days (extendable by 60). Therefore, Statements 1 and 3 are correct.

questions.text: As per the table below showing Production of Major Foodgrains (in Lakh Metric Tonnes) for 2022-23 (4th Advance Estimates), which state has the highest percentage share of Rice production in its Total Foodgrain production?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate Punjab and UP (high Wheat share lowers Rice %). Compare West Bengal (Rice 160, Total 166 ≈ 96%) and Andhra Pradesh (Rice 80, Total 110 ≈ 73%). West Bengal is higher. Worked: WB=160/166≈96.4%; Punjab=130/315≈41.3%; UP=140/510≈27.5%; AP=80/110≈72.7%. Highest is West Bengal.

questions.text: As per the table below showing the Length and Basin Area of four major Indian rivers, which river has the highest ratio of Length (km) to Basin Area (sq km)? Table: River Statistics | River | Length (km) | Basin Area (sq km) | Origin State | |-------|-------------|--------------------|--------------| | Ganga | 2525 | 861452 | Uttarakhand | | Godavari | 1465 | 312812 | Maharashtra | | Krishna | 1400 | 258948 | Maharashtra | | Narmada | 1312 | 98796 | Madhya Pradesh |
questions.solution: Shortcut: The ratio is Length/Area. Look for the combination of relatively high Length and very low Basin Area. Narmada has the smallest Basin Area (approx 99k) by a huge margin while retaining a Length over 1300 km. The other rivers have Basin Areas 2.5x to 8x larger. Narmada wins by inspection without division. Step-by-step: Calculate approximate ratios. Ganga: 2525/861452 ≈ 0.0029. Godavari: 1465/312812 ≈ 0.0047. Krishna: 1400/258948 ≈ 0.0054. Narmada: 1312/98796 ≈ 0.0133. Narmada's ratio is roughly 2.5 to 4.5 times higher than the others.

questions.text: As per the table below showing Net Direct Tax Collections (in Rs Lakh Crore) for the last three Financial Years, what is the approximate Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) over the two-year period from FY 2021-22 to FY 2023-24?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Compute the 2-year growth ratio (Final/Initial) = 19.60 / 13.85 ≈ 1.415. CAGR is the square root of this ratio. Since 1.20² = 1.44 and 1.19² = 1.416, the value is closest to 19%. Worked: CAGR = (19.60/13.85)^(1/2) - 1 = (1.415)^0.5 - 1 ≈ 1.189 - 1 = 0.189 or 18.9% ≈ 19%.

questions.text: As per the table below showing the Target and Actual Growth Rates for the first four Five Year Plans, in which Plan was the shortfall (negative deviation) between the target and actual growth rate the highest? Table: Five Year Plan Growth Rates | Plan | Period | Target Growth (%) | Actual Growth (%) | |------|--------|-------------------|-------------------| | 1st | 1951-56 | 2.1 | 3.6 | | 2nd | 1956-61 | 4.5 | 4.2 | | 3rd | 1961-66 | 5.6 | 2.8 | | 4th | 1969-74 | 5.7 | 3.3 |
questions.solution: Shortcut: Scan the 'Actual vs Target' column pairs. 1st Plan shows a surplus (Actual > Target), so eliminate Option A. For the rest, approximate the gap: 2nd Plan gap ~0.3%; 3rd Plan gap ~2.8% (5.6 - 2.8); 4th Plan gap ~2.4% (5.7 - 3.3). The 3rd Plan gap is visibly the largest. Step-by-step: Calculate deviation (Actual - Target) for each. 1st: 3.6 - 2.1 = +1.5% (Surplus). 2nd: 4.2 - 4.5 = -0.3%. 3rd: 2.8 - 5.6 = -2.8%. 4th: 3.3 - 5.7 = -2.4%. The highest shortfall (most negative) is -2.8% for the Third Plan.

questions.text: A line graph shows India's net exports (in USD billions) from 2015 to 2019: 2015 – 30, 2016 – 28, 2017 – 32, 2018 – 35, 2019 – 34. Using the "average of first and last year" shortcut to estimate the overall trend, what can be inferred?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Average of first (30) and last (34) = 32. Since the average (32) is higher than the first year (30), the overall trend is upward. Full solution: Compute (30+34)/2 = 32. Compare with initial value 30 → increase, indicating net exports have risen overall despite year‑to‑year fluctuations. Hence option B.

questions.text: Consider the following pairs of Ocean Currents and their characteristics: 1. Labrador Current — Cold current, flows southward along the coast of Labrador and Newfoundland. 2. Kuroshio Current — Cold current, flows northward along the coast of Japan. 3. Benguela Current — Warm current, flows northward along the southwestern coast of Africa. 4. East Australian Current — Warm current, flows southward along the east coast of Australia. How many pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the 'Hemisphere Temperature Rule' for quick elimination. In the Northern Hemisphere, currents flowing towards the pole (North) are Warm (Kuroshio, Gulf Stream); towards the equator (South) are Cold (Labrador, California). In the Southern Hemisphere, towards the pole (South) are Warm (East Australian, Brazil); towards equator (North) are Cold (Benguela, Peru/Humboldt). Pair 1: Labrador flows South (Equator-ward) in NH -> Cold (Correct). Pair 2: Kuroshio flows North (Pole-ward) in NH -> Warm (Incorrectly labeled Cold). Pair 3: Benguela flows North (Equator-ward) in SH -> Cold (Incorrectly labeled Warm). Pair 4: East Australian flows South (Pole-ward) in SH -> Warm (Correct). Only Pairs 1 and 4 are correct. Answer: Two pairs.

questions.text: As per the table below showing Quarterly Real GDP Growth (Year-on-Year) for FY 2023-24 (at Constant Prices) released by the National Statistical Office (NSO), how many quarters recorded a growth rate strictly greater than 8.0%?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Scan the 'Growth Rate (%)' column for values where the integer part is 8 and the decimal part is greater than 0 (i.e., > 8.0). Ignore the 7.x entry immediately. Count the 8.x entries: 8.2, 8.1, 8.4 are three quarters. Worked Solution: Q1 (Apr-Jun): 8.2% > 8.0% (Count 1). Q2 (Jul-Sep): 8.1% > 8.0% (Count 2). Q3 (Oct-Dec): 8.4% > 8.0% (Count 3). Q4 (Jan-Mar): 7.8% < 8.0% (Ignore). Total quarters = 3.

questions.text: As per the table below showing Forest Cover and Mangrove Cover (in sq km) for four states as per the India State of Forest Report (ISFR) 2021, which state has the highest ratio of Mangrove Cover to Total Forest Cover? Table: State-wise Forest and Mangrove Cover (ISFR 2021)
questions.solution: Shortcut: Ratio Comparison via Cross-Multiplication (M1/F1 vs M2/F2 → Compare M1×F2 vs M2×F1). Eliminate Andhra Pradesh and Odisha first as their Mangrove cover (< 500 sq km) is negligible compared to Forest cover (> 29,000 sq km), yielding ratios < 2%. Compare top two: Gujarat (M=1103, F=14919) and West Bengal (M=2114, F=16832). Cross-multiply: 1103×16832 ≈ 18.5M vs 2114×14919 ≈ 31.5M. Since 31.5M > 18.5M, West Bengal's ratio is higher. Worked Solution: 1. Gujarat: 1103 / 14919 ≈ 7.39% 2. West Bengal: 2114 / 16832 ≈ 12.56% 3. Andhra Pradesh: 404 / 29784 ≈ 1.36% 4. Odisha: 259 / 52156 ≈ 0.50% Highest ratio is West Bengal (Option B).

questions.text: As per the table below detailing the composition of the three Financial Committees of the Indian Parliament, which committee has members exclusively from the Lok Sabha? Committee | Lok Sabha Members | Rajya Sabha Members | Total Members Estimates Committee | 30 | 0 | 30 Public Accounts Committee | 15 | 7 | 22 Committee on Public Undertakings | 15 | 7 | 22

options.label: D
options.text: Both Public Accounts Committee and Committee on Public Undertakings

questions.solution: Shortcut: Scan the 'Rajya Sabha Members' column for the value '0'. Only the Estimates Committee row shows 0, indicating exclusive Lok Sabha membership. Step-by-step: The Estimates Committee consists of 30 members elected solely from Lok Sabha (Rule 310). The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) and Committee on Public Undertakings (COPU) each comprise 22 members (15 from LS, 7 from RS). Therefore, only the Estimates Committee fits the criterion.

questions.text: According to the chart of India's share in global renewable energy capacity (excluding large hydro) for the years 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023, in which year did India's share increase by the smallest absolute percentage points compared to the previous year?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Look at the differences between consecutive years; the smallest difference gives the answer. The chart data (in %) is: | Year | Share (%) | |------|-----------| | 2020 | 7.2 | | 2021 | 8.0 | | 2022 | 8.5 | | 2023 | 8.6 | Differences: 2021‑2020 = 0.8, 2022‑2021 = 0.5, 2023‑2022 = 0.1. The smallest increase is 0.1% in 2023, which is option index 3. Full solution: 1. Subtract each year's share from the previous year. 2. Identify the minimum positive difference. 3. 2023 shows the least rise (0.1 percentage point), so the correct option is "2023" (index 3).

questions.text: With reference to the special majorities required in the Indian Parliament, which of the following provisions requires a majority of two-thirds of the members present and voting only, without requiring a majority of the total membership of the House?

options.label: A
options.text: Passage of a Constitutional Amendment Bill under Article 368

options.label: B
options.text: Passage of a resolution by Rajya Sabha for creation of All India Services under Article 312

options.label: C
options.text: Removal of a Judge of the Supreme Court under Article 124(2)

options.label: D
options.text: Approval of a Proclamation of National Emergency under Article 352(6)

questions.solution: Shortcut: Elimination by 'Total Membership' clause. Articles 368, 124(2), and 352(6) explicitly mandate 'a majority of the total membership of the House' PLUS 'two-thirds of members present and voting'. Article 312 (Rajya Sabha resolution for All India Services) requires only 'not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting' (Special Majority under Art 249), with no total membership requirement. Worked Solution: 1. Art 368 (Constitutional Amendment): Requires majority of total membership + 2/3rd present and voting. 2. Art 124(2) (Removal of SC Judge): Requires same majority as Art 368 (majority of total membership + 2/3rd present and voting). 3. Art 352(6) (Emergency Approval): Requires same majority as Art 368 (majority of total membership + 2/3rd present and voting). 4. Art 312 (All India Services): Rajya Sabha resolution supported by 'not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting'. No mention of total membership. Hence, Option B is correct.
